title: Graded suppression & de-escalation flow — design notes
body:
Context and motivation:
- We keep getting requests for fewer noisy pages and smarter routing when an SLO-derived alert fires. Current console supports channel-level scheduling and simple channel fallback, but customers need: graded suppression windows, automated de-escalation tiers, and a way to preview impact before turning on policies.
- Goal: design a compact UI flow and underlying policy model that lets product/platform teams express: progressive suppression, timebox de-escalation (auto-suppress after N minutes unless acknowledged), and channel weight/muted-audiences.

High-level requirements (non-exhaustive):
- Policy expresses multiple "suppression tiers" per alert rule (immediate -> partial -> full), each tier with conditions (elapsed time, ack count, incident severity, recent repeats).
- De-escalation: escalate from email -> SMS -> voice, but also support the reverse: start loud, then quiet. Need both progressive escalation and step-down/auto-mute based on ack or triage.
- Tenant defaults + route overrides: org-wide defaults but allow per-project/per-route overrides. Inherit and show effective policy.
- Simulation: run a "what if" simulation on historical signals for a route and show projected page volume reduction and missed-ack risk.
- Auditability: timeline events, who changed which tier and when, rollback to prior policy.

Primary personas:
- Platform engineer (owner of tenant defaults) — cares about predictable volume and SLA with ops team.
- On-call / SRE — cares about clarity of who to contact and how to mute safely during incidents.
- Product manager / PM — wants to tune end-user alert fatigue and prioritize alerts for business-critical routes.

Sketch / UX notes (wireframe fragments):
- Top-level view: "Suppression & De-escalation" tab on Alert Rule config. Header shows rule summary + SLO link + recent alert rate (30d).
- Visual policy timeline (left to right):
  * Tier 0: Immediate actions (notify channels X, Y). Small badges for channels with icons.
  * Tier 1: After 5 min -> reduce to email + slack-thread, remove sms.
  * Tier 2: After 30 min -> mute paging, send daily summary.
  * Each tier card shows condition (time, ack condition, repeat_count), actions, and a simulated impact line (small sparkline).
- Inline controls: quick edit for time windows, toggle on/off, "apply tenant default" link.
- Preview panel on right: shows simulated alert volume and personnel impacted (list of on-call rotations matched). Toggle between 'historical simulation' and 'fast-forward simulation' where you can imagine 5 repeats in 10 min.
- Small affordance: "safeguard" checkbox to prevent complete silence for high-severity incidents (e.g., severity >= P0 always pages at least one channel).

Policy model (notes for backend alignment):
- Represent policy as ordered tiers: [{id, condition, actions, metadata}]. Condition types: elapsed_time, repeat_count, ack_count, severity_threshold, time_of_day, suppression_flag.
- Actions: channel_send (channel_id, template), route_to_rotation, mute_channel, send_digest, webhook.
- Evaluation: first tier applies immediately; on tier transition evaluate conditions and atomically swap active actions. Must persist timeline for audit and simulation.
- Inheritance: final_effective_policy = merge(tenant_default, route_override, rule_override) with conflict resolution: explicit overrides win. Show diffs in UI.

Edge cases and questions (open):
- Q1: What happens to ongoing paged incidents when policy changes mid-incident? Proposed: policy changes only affect new firing events; provide manual "retrospective apply" if owner wants to re-evaluate open incidents.
- Q2: How to surface per-rotation capacity (avoid paging the same engineer repeatedly)? Add throttle/slot limits per-person in later iteration.
- Q3: Should simulation account for human ack latencies? We can allow configurable ack latency distributions per team to model risk.
- Q4: International SMS/voice costs — include cost estimate in preview. This needs costing signals from billing service.

Accessibility and micro-interactions:
- Ensure each tier card is keyboard navigable; tier reorder via drag handle + keyboard alternative.
- Color signals: green = active low-noise, orange = partial suppression, red = immediate page. Also provide patterns beyond color (icons, labels) for color-blind users.

Backlog & next steps (prioritized):
- MVP: implement tiered time-based suppression with simple "ack_count" stop condition + preview (CRT-1425). UI: tier cards + preview panel + apply/rollback. (owner: Maya)
- Follow-up: add tenant inheritance UI and diff view (owner: Ravi).
- Follow-up: historical simulation engine that replays past N days of signals into policy to compute metric: pages avoided vs missed-acks (owner: Evelyn).
- Long-term: per-person throttles, cost estimation, and runbook integrations (PagerDuty/ServiceNow deeper links).

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Product: user can add up to 4 suppression tiers on an alert rule, reorder them, and save.
- UX: preview panel shows estimated page volume delta for past 7 days if the policy had been active.
- Infra: backend policy model accepts tier objects and evaluation engine returns next-action set for given incident state.
- Security/audit: all policy changes are logged with user and timestamp; rollback to prior policy available in UI.

Open implementation notes for engineering sync:
- API: POST /rules/:id/policies with full policy payload; GET returns effective policy with source of truth per field (tenant|route|rule).
- Storage: keep canonical policy history per rule for audit and simulation. Consider storing snapshots to S3 or DB with compact diff.
- Metrics: expose per-rule metric: pages_sent_simulated, pages_sent_actual, ack_rate_post_policy.

Unresolved UX decisions (to discuss in next sync):
- How to label tiers succinctly for non-technical users? (suggestion: "Immediate", "Reduce noise", "Quiet window", "Digest")
- Whether to allow "conditional channel weights" (send to slack 60% of time, email 100%) — might be confusing, postpone to v2.

Notes to self / TODOs before next review:
- Create quick proto in Figma showing tier card interactions and preview panel (Ravi to start).
- Wire up mock simulation data for PM review by EOD next week.
- Draft short user testing script for two SRE teams (oncall + platform) to validate comprehension.

References and inspiration:
- Customer ask thread: slack:#cs-ops (thread ts 1665429)
- Related console doc: confluence:console/notification-patterns (for fallback behavior)

Bottom line summary (one-liner):
Let teams express progressive, timeboxed suppression and automated de-escalation with a compact tiered UI, simulation preview, and tenant-aware defaults so we reduce noisy pages without creating blindspots for critical SLO breaches.

-- end of notes --
